newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to make CEFTA bid this year - president.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to make CEFTA bid this year - president.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said on Tuesday that he expected his country to join the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA), a trading area of former Communist-bloc states, in 1997.

"Lithuania is striving for CEFTA membership and we expect to join this year," Brazauskas said at a joint news conference with Hungarian counterpart Arpad Goncz, who arrived in the Baltic state Tuesday for a three-day official visit.
Brazuaskas added that Lithuania and Hungary expected to sign a free-trade agreement within a few months, clearing the final hurdle between Lithuania and CEFTA membership.
Lithuania has signed free-trade pacts with other CEFTA members, Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia.
As well as orienting itself to central and eastern Europe, Lithuania also aims to boost ties with the West and has applied to become a full member of the European Union (EU).
The president's office said Lithuania exported $10 million worth of goods to Hungary last year and imported $39 million from Hungary. It gave no comparisons with previous years.
Both countries are undergoing the tough transition to a market economy after decades of communist rule.
"Our economic ties are being formed in a favourable envrironment," Goncz said.
Bi-lateral cooperation agreements were also signed in the areas of combatting drug smuggling, terrorism and organized crime.
